key_insight: 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) dynamically regulates tin-perovskite crystallization and, after annealing, is proposed to form interface-passivating species.
engineering_relevance: Combining crystal-growth control and defect passivation offers a route to more efficient, stable lead-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Coordinate PX carbonyl groups with Sn²⁺ to stabilize precursor complexes and moderate supersaturation.
Use controlled crystallization to produce compact, highly crystalline films.
Anneal to induce molecular transformation into proposed amidinium-functionalized species that passivate surface A-site vacancies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 15.18% power conversion efficiency and retention of 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 hours of continuous illumination.
watch_item: The proposed amidinium-forming transformation needs further verification, and the abstract does not specify illumination-test conditions or device-to-device variability.
paper_title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
